entries.title: Not What You've Signed Up For: Compromising Real-World LLM-Integrated Applications with Indirect Prompt Injection
entries.abstract: Introduces indirect prompt injection attacks against LLM-integrated applications, demonstrating how adversaries can remotely control LLMs by injecting prompts into data sources the LLM retrieves.

entries.title: Ignore This Title and HackAPrompt: Exposing Systemic Weaknesses of LLMs through a Global Scale Prompt Hacking Competition
entries.abstract: Presents results from a global prompt hacking competition with 600K+ adversarial prompts, revealing systemic LLM vulnerabilities across multiple models and defense strategies.

entries.title: Jailbroken: How Does LLM Safety Training Fail?
entries.abstract: Analyzes failure modes of LLM safety training, identifying two broad categories: competing objectives and mismatched generalization, demonstrating attacks that exploit each.

entries.title: Universal and Transferable Adversarial Attacks on Aligned Language Models
entries.abstract: Proposes an automated method (GCG) to generate adversarial suffixes that cause aligned LLMs to produce harmful content, with attacks transferring across models including ChatGPT and Claude.

entries.title: Poisoning Language Models During Instruction Tuning
entries.abstract: Shows that adversaries can insert poisoned examples into instruction-tuning datasets, causing models to generate targeted outputs for attacker-chosen triggers.

entries.title: PoisonedRAG: Knowledge Poisoning Attacks to Retrieval-Augmented Generation of Large Language Models
entries.abstract: Demonstrates knowledge poisoning attacks against RAG systems where adversaries inject malicious texts into the knowledge database to manipulate LLM outputs.

entries.title: Extracting Training Data from Large Language Models
entries.abstract: Demonstrates that large language models memorize and can be prompted to emit verbatim training data, including PII, revealing significant privacy risks.

entries.title: Scalable Extraction of Training Data from (Production) Language Models
entries.abstract: Develops a scalable attack to extract over a gigabyte of training data from semi-open and closed models including ChatGPT, at a cost of roughly $200.

entries.title: Stealing Part of a Production Language Model
entries.abstract: Demonstrates that it is possible to steal the embedding projection layer of production LLMs like OpenAI's models through the API, confirming model extraction risks.

entries.title: The Instruction Hierarchy: Training LLMs to Prioritize Privileged Instructions
entries.abstract: Proposes an instruction hierarchy for training LLMs to prioritize system prompts over user prompts over third-party content, as a defense against prompt injection.

entries.title: Llama Guard: LLM-based Input-Output Safeguard for Human-AI Conversations
entries.abstract: Introduces Llama Guard, an LLM-based safeguard model for classifying safety risks in LLM inputs and outputs, achieving strong performance on standard benchmarks.

entries.title: NeMo Guardrails: A Toolkit for Controllable and Safe LLM Applications with Programmable Rails
entries.abstract: Presents NeMo Guardrails, an open-source toolkit for adding programmable safety, security, and privacy rails to LLM-based conversational systems.

entries.title: A Survey on Large Language Model (LLM) Security and Privacy: The Good, The Bad, and The Ugly
entries.abstract: Comprehensive survey covering LLM security and privacy from three perspectives: beneficial applications of LLMs for security, attacks against LLMs, and defensive techniques.

entries.title: Adversarial Attacks and Defenses in Large Language Models: Old and New Threats
entries.abstract: Systematizes adversarial attacks and defenses for LLMs, connecting them to the classical adversarial ML literature while identifying LLM-specific threats.

entries.title: A Comprehensive Survey of Attack Techniques, Implementation, and Mitigation Strategies in Large Language Models
entries.abstract: Surveys attack techniques across the LLM lifecycle including training, fine-tuning, and inference, with comprehensive mitigation strategies.

entries.title: AI Supply Chain Attacks and Mitigations: A Security-Focused Survey
entries.abstract: Surveys the AI/ML supply chain attack surface including model repositories, training pipelines, and dependency risks, with practical mitigations.

entries.title: AgentDojo: A Dynamic Environment to Evaluate Attacks and Defenses for LLM Agents
entries.abstract: Introduces AgentDojo, a framework for evaluating the security of LLM agents against prompt injection and other attacks in realistic tool-use scenarios.

entries.title: InjecAgent: Benchmarking Indirect Prompt Injections in Tool-Integrated LLM Agents
entries.abstract: Presents InjecAgent, a benchmark for evaluating indirect prompt injection attacks against LLM agents that use tools, showing most agents are highly vulnerable.

entries.title: Do Anything Now: Characterizing and Evaluating In-The-Wild Jailbreak Prompts on Large Language Models
entries.abstract: Collects and analyzes 6,387 jailbreak prompts from the wild, developing a comprehensive taxonomy of jailbreak techniques and evaluating their effectiveness.

entries.title: Multi-step Jailbreaking Privacy Attacks on ChatGPT
entries.abstract: Demonstrates multi-step jailbreaking attacks to extract personal information from ChatGPT, showing how sequential prompting can bypass safety measures.

entries.title: A Text Watermark for Large Language Models
entries.abstract: Proposes a watermarking framework for LLM-generated text that embeds a statistically detectable signal without significantly affecting output quality.

entries.title: Can LLMs Keep a Secret? Testing Privacy Implications of Language Models via Contextual Integrity Theory
entries.abstract: Evaluates LLM privacy behavior through the lens of contextual integrity theory, finding significant mismatches between LLM norms and human privacy expectations.

entries.title: Machine Unlearning for Large Language Models: A Survey
entries.abstract: Surveys machine unlearning techniques for LLMs including methods for forgetting specific training data, complying with data deletion requests, and maintaining model utility.

entries.title: Red Teaming Language Models to Reduce Harms: Methods, Scaling Behaviors, and Lessons Learned
entries.abstract: Describes Anthropic's early red teaming methodology for language models, documenting methods, scaling behaviors, and lessons for identifying harmful outputs.

entries.title: Garak: A Framework for Security Probing Large Language Models
entries.abstract: Presents garak, an open-source framework for systematically probing LLM vulnerabilities including prompt injection, data leakage, and toxicity generation.

entries.title: R-Judge: Benchmarking Safety Risk Awareness for LLM Agents
entries.abstract: Introduces R-Judge benchmark for evaluating whether LLM agents can identify safety risks in agentic scenarios involving tool use and multi-step reasoning.

entries.title: OWASP Top 10 for Large Language Model Applications
entries.abstract: The definitive OWASP guide identifying the top 10 most critical security risks in LLM applications, with descriptions, examples, and mitigation strategies.

entries.title: NIST Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework (AI RMF 1.0)
authors: National Institute of Standards and Technology
entries.abstract: Voluntary framework for managing risks in AI systems across the lifecycle, organized into Govern, Map, Measure, and Manage functions.

entries.title: MITRE ATLAS: Adversarial Threat Landscape for AI Systems
entries.abstract: Knowledge base of adversarial tactics, techniques, and case studies for AI systems, modeled on the ATT&CK framework for cybersecurity.

entries.title: OWASP AI Security and Privacy Guide
entries.abstract: Comprehensive guide for AI security and privacy including threat analysis, controls, and regulatory mapping for AI systems.

entries.title: Anthropic: Many-shot Jailbreaking
entries.abstract: Reveals many-shot jailbreaking, a technique exploiting long context windows by including many examples of harmful Q&A pairs to override safety training.

entries.title: Constitutional AI: Harmlessness from AI Feedback
entries.abstract: Introduces Constitutional AI (CAI), a method for training AI systems to be harmless using a set of principles (a constitution) and AI-generated feedback, reducing reliance on human red teamers.

entries.title: Prompt Injection Attack Against LLM-Integrated Applications
entries.abstract: First comprehensive survey of prompt injection attacks against LLM-integrated applications, categorizing attacks and defenses with a unified framework.

entries.title: Rebuff: Self-Hardening Prompt Injection Detector
entries.abstract: Open-source tool designed to detect and prevent prompt injection attacks using multiple detection methods including heuristics, LLM-based analysis, and canary tokens.

entries.title: PyRIT: Python Risk Identification Toolkit for Generative AI
entries.abstract: Microsoft's open-source framework for red teaming generative AI systems, supporting automated prompt generation, attack strategies, and scoring of AI responses.

entries.title: Sleeper Agents: Training Deceptive LLMs that Persist Through Safety Training
entries.abstract: Demonstrates that LLMs can be trained with deceptive behaviors (sleeper agents) that persist through standard safety training including RLHF, posing risks for backdoor attacks.

entries.title: DP-SGD for Fine-Tuning Foundation Models: A Privacy-Utility Trade-off Study
entries.abstract: Investigates applying differentially private stochastic gradient descent to fine-tune large foundation models, characterizing the privacy-utility trade-off.

entries.title: Tensor Trust: Interpretable Prompt Injection Attacks from an Online Game
entries.abstract: Uses data from an online game (Tensor Trust) where players compete to craft prompt injections and defenses, creating a large dataset of human-generated attacks.

entries.title: OWASP LLM AI Security & Governance Checklist
entries.abstract: Practical checklist for organizations deploying LLMs covering security, governance, legal, and regulatory considerations with actionable steps.

entries.title: Federated Fine-Tuning of LLMs on the Very Edge: The Good, the Bad, the Ugly
entries.abstract: Examines federated learning approaches for fine-tuning LLMs on edge devices, analyzing privacy guarantees, communication efficiency, and security trade-offs.

entries.title: TrojLLM: A Black-box Trojan Prompt Attack on Large Language Models
entries.abstract: Proposes TrojLLM, a black-box attack that generates universal trojan prompts to compromise LLMs without access to model internals.

entries.title: LoRA Fine-Tuning Efficiently Undoes Safety Training in Llama 2-Chat
entries.abstract: Shows that LoRA fine-tuning with as few as 100 examples can remove safety guardrails from Llama 2-Chat, raising concerns about fine-tuning access to aligned models.

entries.title: Assessing the Brittleness of Safety Alignment via Pruning and Low-Rank Modifications
entries.abstract: Demonstrates that safety alignment in LLMs is brittle and can be undermined through simple weight pruning or low-rank modifications without any fine-tuning data.

entries.title: ConfusedPilot: Confused Deputy Attacks Against RAG-based Code Assistants
entries.abstract: Introduces confused deputy attacks against RAG-based code assistants like GitHub Copilot, where poisoned code repositories manipulate assistant outputs.

entries.title: Toolformer: Language Models Can Teach Themselves to Use Tools
entries.abstract: Demonstrates how LLMs can learn to use external tools (APIs, search engines, calculators) through self-supervised learning, foundational for understanding tool-use security.

entries.title: Identifying and Mitigating the Security Risks of Generative AI
entries.venue: Foundations and Trends in Privacy and Security
entries.abstract: Comprehensive treatment of generative AI security risks across the ML lifecycle with a focus on practical mitigations and deployment considerations.

entries.title: The AI Security Pyramid of Pain
entries.abstract: Adapts David Bianco's Pyramid of Pain framework to AI security, categorizing AI threats by how difficult they are for adversaries to change.

entries.title: Securing LLM Systems Against Prompt Injection
entries.abstract: Proposes defense mechanisms against prompt injection in LLM systems including isolation-based approaches, input/output filtering, and detection methods.

entries.title: Adversarial Machine Learning: A Taxonomy and Terminology of Attacks and Mitigations (NIST AI 100-2e2025)
entries.abstract: NIST's authoritative taxonomy of adversarial ML attacks and mitigations covering evasion, poisoning, privacy, and abuse attacks against AI systems.

entries.title: Google DeepMind: Gemini Security Assessment and Red Team Evaluation
entries.abstract: Describes Google's approach to red teaming Gemini models, including automated and human evaluation methods for safety and security.

entries.title: LLM Agents Can Autonomously Hack Websites
entries.abstract: Demonstrates that LLM agents can autonomously perform web hacking tasks including SQL injection, XSS, and CSRF attacks without human guidance.

entries.title: Pandora's White-Box: Precise Training Data Detection and Extraction in Large Language Models
entries.abstract: Develops precise methods for detecting and extracting training data from LLMs when white-box access is available, with implications for copyright and privacy.

entries.title: OWASP Top 10 for Agentic AI Applications
entries.abstract: Identifies the top 10 security risks specific to agentic AI applications including excessive agency, unsafe tool execution, and inadequate oversight.

entries.title: From Prompt Injections to SQL Injection Attacks: How Protected is Your LLM-Integrated Web Application?
entries.abstract: Demonstrates how prompt injection can be chained with traditional web attacks (SQL injection, XSS) in LLM-integrated applications.

entries.title: Model Context Protocol (MCP): Security Considerations and Best Practices
entries.abstract: Documentation and analysis of security considerations for the Model Context Protocol, covering authentication, authorization, and tool sandboxing.

entries.title: Benchmarking and Defending Against Indirect Prompt Injection Attacks on Large Language Models
entries.abstract: Provides a benchmark for indirect prompt injection attacks and evaluates several defense strategies including perplexity-based detection and sandwich defense.

entries.title: AI Security: A Comprehensive Guide to Threats, Defenses, and Best Practices
entries.abstract: Comprehensive practitioner guide covering AI/ML security from an architectural risk analysis perspective, with practical defense patterns.

entries.title: Security of AI-Based Code Generation Tools: A Multi-Perspective Study
entries.abstract: Examines security implications of AI code generation tools, analyzing vulnerability introduction patterns and mitigation strategies.

entries.title: HarmBench: A Standardized Evaluation Framework for Automated Red Teaming and Robust Refusal
entries.abstract: Introduces HarmBench, a standardized framework for evaluating automated red teaming methods and robust refusal in LLMs with a comprehensive behavior taxonomy.

entries.title: ISO/IEC 42001:2023 - Artificial Intelligence Management System
entries.abstract: International standard specifying requirements for establishing, implementing, maintaining and continually improving an AI management system within organizations.

entries.title: AutoDAN: Generating Stealthy Jailbreak Prompts on Aligned Large Language Models
entries.abstract: Proposes AutoDAN, a method for automatically generating stealthy jailbreak prompts that are semantically meaningful and can bypass perplexity-based defenses.

entries.title: Tree of Attacks: Jailbreaking Black-Box LLMs with Auto-Generated Subtrees
entries.abstract: Introduces TAP using an LLM to iteratively refine jailbreak prompts against black-box target models with high success rates.

entries.title: GPT-4 Is Too Smart To Be Safe: Stealthy Chat with LLMs via Cipher
entries.abstract: Demonstrates that LLMs can be jailbroken using cipher-based encoding, bypassing safety training designed for natural language.

entries.title: DecodingTrust: A Comprehensive Assessment of Trustworthiness in GPT Models
entries.abstract: Comprehensive trustworthiness evaluation of GPT models across 8 dimensions including toxicity, bias, robustness, privacy, fairness, and machine ethics.

entries.title: Purple Llama CyberSecEval: A Secure Coding Benchmark for Language Models
entries.abstract: Introduces CyberSecEval, a benchmark for evaluating the cybersecurity risks of LLM code generation, including insecure code suggestions.

entries.title: BadChain: Backdoor Chain-of-Thought Prompting for Large Language Models
entries.abstract: Demonstrates backdoor attacks on chain-of-thought reasoning in LLMs where poisoned demonstrations cause incorrect reasoning chains.

entries.title: PAIR: Prompt Automatic Iterative Refinement for Jailbreaking LLMs
entries.abstract: Uses an attacker LLM to automatically generate jailbreak prompts through iterative refinement achieving high success with only black-box access.

entries.title: GPT in Sheep's Clothing: The Risk of Customized GPTs
entries.abstract: Analyzes security risks of custom GPTs in the OpenAI GPT Store including prompt leakage, data exfiltration, and malicious GPTs.

entries.title: Vigil: LLM Prompt Injection Detection and Defense Toolkit
entries.abstract: Open-source scanner for detecting prompt injections using vector similarity, YARA rules, text classifiers, and canary tokens.

entries.title: Guardrails AI: Input/Output Guards for LLM Applications
entries.abstract: Framework for adding structural, type, and quality guarantees to LLM outputs with validators for PII, toxicity, code security, and factual accuracy.

entries.title: LLM Guard: Security Toolkit for LLM Interactions
entries.abstract: Comprehensive toolkit for sanitizing LLM prompts and outputs, detecting prompt injection, PII leakage, toxic content, and code vulnerabilities.

entries.title: The Emerged Security and Privacy of LLM Agent: A Survey with Case Studies
entries.abstract: Surveys security and privacy challenges specific to LLM-based agents, covering agent architectures, attack surfaces, and defense mechanisms.

entries.title: Adaptive Attacks Break Defenses Against LLM Jailbreaking
entries.abstract: Shows that adaptive adversaries can bypass most proposed jailbreak defenses, highlighting the arms race between attacks and defenses.

entries.title: How Johnny Can Persuade LLMs to Jailbreak Them: Rethinking Persuasion to Challenge AI Safety
entries.abstract: Applies social science persuasion techniques to jailbreak LLMs, showing high attack success rates using persuasion taxonomy.

entries.title: Model Context Protocol (MCP): Specification
entries.abstract: Open protocol specification for connecting AI models to external data sources and tools, enabling standardized tool use with security considerations.

entries.title: Anthropic's Responsible Scaling Policy
entries.abstract: Framework defining AI Safety Levels (ASL) for evaluating and managing risks from increasingly capable AI systems.

entries.title: OpenAI: Preparedness Framework (Beta)
entries.abstract: OpenAI's approach to tracking, evaluating, forecasting, and protecting against catastrophic risks of frontier AI models.

entries.title: EU AI Act: Regulation on Artificial Intelligence
entries.venue: Official Journal of the European Union
entries.abstract: The EU's comprehensive AI regulation establishing risk-based categories, conformity assessments, and requirements for high-risk AI systems.

entries.title: Google: Secure AI Framework (SAIF)
entries.abstract: Google's conceptual framework for secure AI systems with six core elements covering security foundations, detection, automation, and contextualization.

entries.title: Microsoft AI Red Team: Lessons Learned and Best Practices
entries.abstract: Shares lessons from Microsoft's AI red team operations including methodology, tooling, common failure modes, and best practices.

entries.title: LLM Agents Can Autonomously Exploit One-day Vulnerabilities
entries.abstract: Shows that LLM agents (GPT-4) can autonomously exploit real-world one-day vulnerabilities given CVE descriptions, achieving 87% success rate.

entries.title: Adversarial Attacks on Multimodal Agents
entries.abstract: Demonstrates adversarial attacks on multimodal agents that take actions in digital environments, showing visual perturbations can hijack agent behavior.

entries.title: SWE-agent: Agent-Computer Interfaces Enable Automated Software Engineering
entries.abstract: Demonstrates autonomous coding agents that interact with computer interfaces to solve software engineering tasks, raising questions about agent containment.

entries.title: TrustLLM: Trustworthiness in Large Language Models
entries.abstract: Comprehensive study of LLM trustworthiness across truthfulness, safety, fairness, robustness, privacy, and machine ethics with benchmarks.

entries.title: On the Societal Impact of Open Foundation Models
entries.abstract: Analyzes the societal impacts of open-weight foundation models, including security implications of open vs closed model access.

entries.title: Poisoning Web-Scale Training Datasets is Practical
entries.abstract: Demonstrates practical attacks to poison web-scale datasets like LAION by purchasing expired domains, affecting 0.01% of a dataset for under $60.

entries.title: Visual Adversarial Examples Jailbreak Aligned Large Language Models
entries.abstract: Shows adversarial images can jailbreak multimodal LLMs that are robust to text-only attacks, bypassing alignment through the visual channel.

entries.title: Are Aligned Neural Networks Adversarially Aligned?
entries.abstract: Evaluates whether multimodal LLMs aligned to refuse harmful text requests also refuse harmful image-based requests, finding significant gaps.

entries.title: Generative AI Security: Theories and Practices
entries.abstract: Comprehensive textbook covering generative AI security from foundations to advanced topics including LLM threats, defenses, privacy, and governance.

entries.title: ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models
entries.abstract: Foundational work on the ReAct paradigm for LLM agents that interleave reasoning and tool-use actions, enabling complex task completion with security implications.

entries.title: Voyager: An Open-Ended Embodied Agent with Large Language Models
entries.abstract: Demonstrates a continuously learning LLM agent in Minecraft that writes and executes code, highlighting autonomous operation and containment challenges.

entries.title: SafetyBench: Evaluating the Safety of Large Language Models
entries.abstract: Large-scale safety evaluation benchmark with 11,435 multiple-choice questions across 7 safety categories in both Chinese and English.

entries.title: Can Sensitive Information Be Deleted From LLMs? Objectives for Defending Against Extraction Attacks
entries.abstract: Evaluates methods for deleting sensitive information from trained LLMs, finding current unlearning approaches insufficient against determined adversaries.

entries.title: WildGuard: Open One-Stop Moderation Tools for Safety Risks, Jailbreaks, and Refusals of LLMs
entries.abstract: Open-source moderation tool for detecting safety risks in LLM interactions, trained on a diverse dataset of harmful and benign prompts.

entries.title: StrongREJECT: A Comprehensive Evaluation of LLM Safety Refusal Behaviors
entries.abstract: Introduces StrongREJECT, a high-quality evaluation benchmark for measuring how well LLMs refuse harmful requests.

entries.title: OWASP Threat Dragon: AI-Aware Threat Modeling Tool
entries.abstract: Open-source threat modeling tool supporting AI/ML system threat models, data flow diagrams, and STRIDE methodology for GenAI applications.

entries.title: CISA: Roadmap for Artificial Intelligence
entries.abstract: CISA's strategic roadmap for AI covering responsible use, assuring AI systems, securing AI adoption, and collaborating on AI governance.

entries.title: Prompt Stealing Attacks Against Text-to-Image Generation Models
entries.abstract: Demonstrates attacks that steal the prompts used to generate images from text-to-image models, raising IP and privacy concerns.

entries.title: The Shadow Alignment: The Risks of RLHF to LLM Alignment
entries.abstract: Shows that RLHF can introduce shadow alignment where models exhibit harmful behaviors not present in the base model.

entries.title: Confidential Computing for AI Workloads: Survey and Best Practices
entries.abstract: Surveys confidential computing technologies (SGX, SEV, TDX) applied to AI workloads covering secure training, inference, and multi-party computation.

entries.title: MetaBackdoor: Exploiting Positional Encoding as a Backdoor Attack Surface in LLMs
entries.abstract: Backdoor attacks pose a serious security threat to large language models (LLMs), which are increasingly deployed as general-purpose assistants in safety- and privacy-critical applications. Existing LLM backdoors rely primarily on content-based triggers, requiring explicit modification of the input text. In this work, we show that this assumption is unnecessary and limiting. entries.abstract: We introduce a reusable framework for auditing whether LLM attack benchmarks collectively cover the threat surface: a 4$\times$6 Target $\times$ Technique matrix grounded in STRIDE, constructed from a 507-leaf taxonomy -- 401 data-populated and 106 threat-model-derived leaves -- of inference-time attacks extracted from 932 arXiv security studies (2023--2026). entries.title: Model-Agnostic Lifelong LLM Safety via Externalized Attack-Defense Co-Evolution
entries.abstract: Large language models remain vulnerable to adversarial prompts that elicit harmful outputs. Existing safety paradigms typically couple red-teaming and post-training in a closed, policy-centric loop, causing attack discovery to suffer from rapid saturation and limiting the exposure of novel failure modes, while leaving defenses inefficient, rigid, and difficult to transfer across victim models. entries.title: Quantifying LLM Safety Degradation Under Repeated Attacks Using Survival Analysis
entries.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed in a wide range of applications, yet remain vulnerable to adversarial jailbreak attacks that circumvent their safety guardrails. Existing evaluation frameworks typically report binary success/failure metrics, failing to capture the temporal dynamics of how attacks succeed under persistent adversarial pressure. entries.title: REALISTA: Realistic Latent Adversarial Attacks that Elicit LLM Hallucinations
entries.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) achieve strong performance across many tasks but remain vulnerable to hallucinations, motivating the need for realistic adversarial prompts that elicit such failures. We formulate hallucination elicitation as a constrained optimization problem, where the goal is to find semantically coherent adversarial prompts that are equivalent to benign user prompts. entries.title: BadSKP: Backdoor Attacks on Knowledge Graph-Enhanced LLMs with Soft Prompts
entries.abstract: Recent knowledge graph (KG)-enhanced large language models (LLMs) move beyond purely textual knowledge augmentation by encoding retrieved subgraphs into continuous soft prompts via graph neural networks, introducing a graph-conditioned channel that operates alongside the standard text interface. However, existing backdoor attacks are largely designed for the textual channel, and their effectiveness against this dual-channel architecture remains unclear. entries.abstract: Backdoor vulnerabilities widely exist in the fine-tuning of large language models(LLMs). Most backdoor poisoning methods operate mainly at the token level and lack deeper semantic manipulation, which limits stealthiness. entries.title: FlowSteer: Prompt-Only Workflow Steering Exposes Planning-Time Vulnerabilities in Multi-Agent LLM Systems
entries.abstract: Multi-agent systems (MAS) powered by large language models (LLMs) increasingly adopt planner--executor architectures, where planners convert prompts into subtasks, roles, dependencies, and routing paths. This flexibility enables adaptive coordination, but exposes an attack surface in workflow formation: prompts can shape agent organization without modifying MAS infrastructure. entries.title: Benchmarking LLM-Based Static Analysis for Secure Smart Contract Development: Reliability, Limitations, and Potential Hybrid Solutions
entries.abstract: The irreversible nature of blockchain transactions makes the identification of smart contract vulnerabilities an essential requirement for secure system development. While Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly integrated into developer workflows, their reliability as autonomous security auditors remains unproven. entries.title: MCPShield: Content-Aware Attack Detection for LLM Agent Tool-Call Traffic
entries.abstract: The Model Context Protocol (MCP) has become a widely adopted interface for LLM agents to invoke external tools, yet learned monitoring of MCP tool-call traffic remains underexplored. entries.title: The Granularity Mismatch in Agent Security: Argument-Level Provenance Solves Enforcement and Isolates the LLM Reasoning Bottleneck
entries.abstract: Tool-using LLM agents must act on untrusted webpages, emails, files, and API outputs while issuing privileged tool calls. Existing defenses often mediate trust at the granularity of an entire tool invocation, forcing a brittle choice in mixed-trust workflows: allow external content to influence a call and risk hijacked destinations or commands, or quarantine the call and block benign retrieval-then-act behavior. entries.title: The Art of the Jailbreak: Formulating Jailbreak Attacks for LLM Security Beyond Binary Scoring
entries.abstract: Jailbreak attacks -- adversarial prompts that bypass LLM alignment through purely linguistic manipulation -- pose a growing operational security threat, yet the field lacks large-scale, reproducible infrastructure for generating, categorizing, and evaluating them systematically. This paper addresses that gap with three contributions. (1) Large-scale compositional jailbreak dataset. entries.title: Few-Shot Truly Benign DPO Attack for Jailbreaking LLMs
entries.abstract: Fine-tuning APIs make frontier LLMs easy to customize, but they can also weaken safety alignment during fine-tuning. While prior work shows that benign supervised fine-tuning (SFT) can reduce refusal behavior, deployed fine-tuning pipelines increasingly support preference-based objectives, whose safety risks remain less understood. entries.title: LLM-Agnostic Semantic Representation Attack
entries.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) increasingly employ alignment techniques to prevent harmful outputs. Despite these safeguards, attackers can circumvent them by crafting adversarial prompts. Predominant token-level optimization methods primarily rely on optimizing for exact affirmative templates (e.g., ``\textit{Sure, here is...}''). entries.title: When LLMs Team Up: A Coordinated Attack Framework for Automated Cyber Intrusions
entries.abstract: Automated intrusion-style workflows require LLM agents to reason over partial observations, tool outputs, and executable artifacts under bounded budgets. A single LLM instance often compresses evidence extraction, planning, execution, and validation into one context, which increases the risk of context drift and error propagation. entries.title: PASA: A Principled Embedding-Space Watermarking Approach for LLM-Generated Text under Semantic-Invariant Attacks
entries.abstract: Watermarking for large language models (LLMs) is a promising approach for detecting LLM-generated text and enabling responsible deployment. However, existing watermarking methods are often vulnerable to semantic-invariant attacks, such as paraphrasing. We propose PASA, a principled, robust, and distortion-free watermarking algorithm that embeds and detects a watermark at the semantic level. entries.title: CyBiasBench: Benchmarking Bias in LLM Agents for Cyber-Attack Scenarios
entries.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed as autonomous agents in offensive cybersecurity. In this paper, we reveal an interesting phenomenon: different agents exhibit distinct attack patterns. entries.title: Insider Attacks in Multi-Agent LLM Consensus Systems
entries.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed in multi-agent systems where agents communicate in natural language to solve tasks jointly. A key capability in such systems is consensus formation, where agents iteratively exchange messages and update decisions to reach a shared outcome. entries.title: Towards Security-Auditable LLM Agents: A Unified Graph Representation
entries.abstract: LLM-based agentic systems are rapidly evolving to perform complex autonomous tasks through dynamic tool invocation, stateful memory management, and multi-agent collaboration. entries.title: Pop Quiz Attack: Black-box Membership Inference Attacks Against Large Language Models
entries.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) show strong performance across many applications, but their ability to memorize and potentially reveal training data raises serious privacy concerns. We introduce the PopQuiz Attack, a black-box membership inference attack that tests whether a model can recall specific training examples. entries.title: Correct Code, Vulnerable Dependencies: A Large Scale Measurement Study of LLM-Specified Library Versions
